events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.
I'll check what's in the workspace first so the app fits whatever is already there.

events.content:
The book tracker is built and working. Run npm start and open http://127.0.0.1:3000.

- Home page: shows "Currently reading" (each book has a "Mark finished" button) and "Finished" (newest first, with the date you finished). Below those is a form to add a book with title, author and notes. Title and author are required.
- Book page: clicking a book opens it at /books/<id>, showing the title, author, notes and whether you're reading it or finished it. That address is the link you'd send someone.
- Storage: books are saved to data/books.json, which I added to .gitignore. No database, no accounts, and no packages beyond Node's own.

Testing: npm test passed all 4 tests. They cover the empty first run, adding a book, opening its page, marking it finished, the books still being there after a restart, the form rejecting a missing title or author, and unknown books returning a not-found page. I also ran the real server, added a book, restarted it, and the book's page and JSON entry were still there.

Things to know:
- Sharing links: by default the app only accepts connections from your own computer, so a link you send won't open for anyone else. To share, run it with HOST=0.0.0.0 so other machines can reach it. There are no accounts, so anyone who can reach the app can also add books and mark them finished.
- Notes: you can only write notes when you add a book; there's no way to edit them afterwards yet.
- Settings: PORT and BOOKS_FILE change the port and where the JSON file is saved.

The code is in server.js, src/store.js (saving to the file), src/app.js (pages and form handling) and test/app.test.js.
